info.name: Font
info.comment: Provides font management functionality and hosts the Font class.

description.p: The Font module maintains the system font database and provides query functions for resolving font family names, styles, file paths and metadata. Fixed-size bitmap fonts are recognised through the Windows .fon format, while TrueType fonts are scanned as scalable font resources.

Bitmap fonts can be opened and drawn directly by the Font class. Scalable TrueType rendering is handled by the Vector module and VectorText class; the Font module supplies the database information that allows those fonts to be selected.
For a thorough introduction to typesetting history and terminology as it applies to computing, we recommend visiting Google Fonts Knowledge page: https://fonts.google.com/knowledge

function.name: CharWidth
function.comment: Returns the width of a character.

input.param: The font to use for calculating the character width.
A Unicode character value.

description.p: Returns the pixel width of a bitmap font character. Char is interpreted as a Unicode character value. Bitmap fonts provide a maximum of 256 glyph slots; unsupported characters fall back to the font's default character.
The font's GlyphSpacing value is not included in the returned width. If Font is NULL or has no character table, the result is 0.

function.result: The pixel width of the character, or 0 if it cannot be measured.

function.name: RefreshFonts
function.comment: Refreshes the system font list with up-to-date font information.

input.param: Optional. Overrides the default fonts:fonts.cfg location that the font database is saved to.
Optional flags.

description.p: Scans the fonts: volume and rebuilds the font database. The tailored options in fonts:options.cfg, such as family aliases and metric modifiers, are merged into the database again once the refresh is complete.

Refreshing fonts can take an extensive amount of time because each font file must be analysed for family, style, metric and metadata information. The font database is saved to fonts:fonts.cfg on completion, unless an alternative location is specified in Path.
Fonts registered with RegisterFont are private to the process and are neither cleared nor saved by a refresh.

If the SCAN_HOST flag is set, the host's native font folders are scanned for scalable fonts after the fonts: volume. On Linux the folders are, in order: $XDG_DATA_HOME/fonts (defaulting to ~/.local/share/fonts), ~/.fonts, the fonts folder of each $XDG_DATA_DIRS entry (defaulting to /usr/local/share:/usr/share), /usr/share/fonts and /usr/local/share/fonts. The folders are scanned recursively for ttf, otf, ttc and otc files, and host fonts are recorded by their absolute paths. If a host family style is found in more than one folder, the first folder in the list above takes precedence. Every face in a collection is scanned. For faces after the first, the zero-based index is stored in the FaceIndex:Style key, where Style is the corresponding style name, and is returned by SelectFontFace. A style without this key uses face zero. Host scanning is not supported on other platforms at this time, and the flag is ignored there.

Host fonts are saved to their own database at user:config/host_fonts.cfg, regardless of Path, so that the fonts: database remains exclusive to Kotuku's fonts. The host database is merged into the font database after it is saved, and before fonts:options.cfg. If SCAN_HOST is not set, the host database from an earlier scan is merged instead, if it exists. Families provided by the fonts: volume take precedence and are never mixed with host files of the same name. On module initialisation, a missing host database is built independently of an existing fonts: database; a failure to save that per-user cache does not prevent font loading. To stop using host fonts, delete user:config/host_fonts.cfg and refresh the fonts.

Host font folders can hold thousands of files, so expect a host scan to take considerably longer than a standard refresh. Host fonts that are subsequently removed will remain in the host database until the next host scan.
Each family is recorded as a group, keyed by family name, in which each style name refers to the file that provides it. The following keys describe the family as a whole:

types.type: A sorted CSV list of the family's style names.
Yes if the family is an outline font. Bitmap families omit this key.
Yes if the family is a variable font.

A CSV list of the point sizes available. Bitmap families record their strikes. A scalable family only has this key if it is defined in fonts:options.cfg, which restricts the family to the listed sizes.

The family's classification: Serif, Sans, Mono, Script, Display or Symbol. The class is read from the OS/2 PANOSE and family class data of outline fonts and the pitch and family field of bitmap fonts. If an outline font does not declare a class, its serifs are measured on the capital I and T. The key is omitted if the class cannot be determined.
Variable families only: a CSV list of axis tags, e.g. wght,wdth.
Variable families only: the range of each axis as tag:min:default:max, e.g. wght:100:400:900,wdth:62.5:100:100. The ranges of all files in the family are combined.
A sorted CSV list of the OpenType layout features found in the GSUB and GPOS tables, e.g. kern,liga,tnum. A legacy kern table is reported as kern.

The percentage of each character set that is mapped by the family, as id:percent, e.g. basic-latin:100,greek:89. Percentages are rounded down, so 100 indicates complete coverage, and a set with any coverage reports at least 1. Sets that have no coverage are omitted. The set ids are basic-latin, latin-1, latin-ext-a, latin-ext-b, pasifika (macron vowels and the ʻokina), vietnamese, greek, cyrillic, ipa, arrows-math, box-drawing, emoji and cjk.
The count of characters mapped by the family's largest file.

description.p: Bitmap fonts are treated as Latin-1 for coverage purposes, which matches how the Font class maps their characters.

function.name: RegisterFont
function.comment: Makes a font file available to the running process.

input.param: The location of the font file.
Optional, returns the family name of the registered font.

description.p: Registers a scalable font file, such as a TrueType or OpenType file, so that its family can be referenced by name in the same way as an installed font. This allows an application to use fonts that are distributed with it, without installing them to the fonts: volume.

The family and style names are read from the file. A variable font registers each of its named styles. The resolved family name is returned in Family and can be used with the VectorText.Face field, SelectFont and ResolveFamilyName. Registering further files for the same family adds their styles to it, with the most recently registered file taking precedence for any style that is provided more than once.

Registered fonts are private to the running process. They are not saved to the font database, do not appear in the font lists that are built from fonts:fonts.cfg and are unaffected by RefreshFonts. A registered family takes precedence over an installed family of the same name. Registrations last until the Font module is expunged; there is no means of removing them.

result.error: Operation successful.
The file is not a recognised font format.
The file is not a scalable font.
Access to the font database was denied, or the object does not exist.

function.name: ResolveFamilyName
function.comment: Convert a CSV family string to a single family name.
function.prototype: ERR fnt::ResolveFamilyName(STRVIEW String, STRVIEW * Result, STRVIEW * Alias)

input.param: A CSV family string to resolve.
The resolved family name is returned in this parameter.
Optional. Returns the name of the alias that the family was resolved through, or an empty string.

description.p: Converts a CSV family string to one resolved family name. String is parsed from left to right, with each family name or wildcard tested against the font database in order. If a single asterisk is used to terminate the list, the system default is returned when no earlier name matches.

Individual names may use the common wildcards ? and *; for example, Times New * can match Times New Roman if it is available. Families registered with RegisterFont are tested before the font database.

A family can be an alias of another, as declared by the Alias key in fonts:options.cfg. Aliases are followed to the family that they refer to, and the name of the first alias that was matched is returned in Alias. The alias's group in the font configuration can then be consulted for its Style and metric options. Alias is empty if the family was not resolved through an alias.
The returned Result and Alias are borrowed storage. Copy them immediately if they need to survive a later font database refresh.

result.error: Operation successful.
It was not possible to resolve the String to a known font family.
Access to the font database was denied, or the object does not exist.
GetField() failed to retrieve a field value
Function call missing argument value(s)

function.name: SelectFont
function.comment: Searches for a 'best fitting' font file, based on family name and style.
function.prototype: ERR fnt::SelectFont(STRVIEW Name, STRVIEW Style, STRING * Path, FMETA * Meta)

input.param: The name of a font face to search for (case insensitive).
The preferred style, e.g. Bold or Italic.
The location of the best-matching font file is returned in this parameter.
Optional, returns additional meta information about the font file.

description.p: Resolves a font family Name and preferred Style to a font file path. The family name must exist in the font database or have been registered with RegisterFont.

The Style can be a style name such as Semi Bold Italic, or a style string with descriptors such as weight=Medium;width=Condensed;italic=yes. The weight, width, italic and slant descriptors are used to choose the file; other descriptors are ignored here. See the VectorText FontStyle field for the full syntax.

If the requested style is unavailable, the nearest available style is chosen with the CSS font matching order: width first, then italic, then weight. For instance, a request for Semi Bold on a family that only provides Regular, Italic, Bold and Bold Italic resolves to Bold. Style names that do not describe a weight, width or slope are only chosen if the family has no other styles.

Families registered with RegisterFont are searched first and resolved exclusively from their registered files, so a private family will shadow a system family of the same name. The Meta result for a private family includes the HIDDEN flag.

result.error: Operation successful.
Unable to find a suitable font.
Access to the font database was denied, or the object does not exist.
Failed to create a new memory block
Function call missing argument value(s)

function.name: SelectFontFace
function.comment: Selects a font file and its face within a collection.
function.prototype: ERR fnt::SelectFontFace(STRVIEW Name, STRVIEW Style, STRING * Path, FMETA * Meta, INT * FaceIndex)
function.tiriPrototype: err, Path:str, Meta:num, FaceIndex:num = SelectFontFace(Name:str, Style:str)

input.param: The font family name, matched case insensitively.
The preferred style name or style descriptors, as accepted by SelectFont.
The selected font file path.
Optional, receives the font metadata flags.
Optional, receives the zero-based face index within the selected file.

description.p: Uses the same family and style matching as SelectFont, and also returns the zero-based face index needed to open font collections with FreeType. File paths remain ordinary paths without an encoded index. Fonts whose database entries have no face index use face zero.

function.name: StringWidth
function.comment: Returns the pixel width of any given string in relation to a font's settings.
function.prototype: INT fnt::StringWidth(objFont * Font, STRVIEW String, INT Chars)

input.param: An initialised font object.
The string to be calculated.
The maximum number of characters to measure, or -1 to measure the entire string.

description.p: Calculates the pixel width of String using the supplied Font object's current metrics and spacing settings. Line feeds are handled by measuring each line independently and returning the width of the longest line.
Word wrapping is not applied, even if WrapEdge has been set on the Font object.

function.result: The pixel width of the string, or 0 if Font is NULL, uninitialised or String is empty.
